title: Ajinkya Rahane Joins Amsterdam Flames for Inaugural European T20 Premier League
excerpt: Days after retiring from all formats of cricket, the former India captain signs with Steve Waugh's franchise for Europe's newest T20 league starting August 26.
body:
• Ajinkya Rahane has signed with the Amsterdam Flames as a marquee player for the inaugural European T20 Premier League (ETPL)
  • The move comes just days after Rahane announced his retirement from all forms of cricket on July 30
  • The ETPL begins August 26 with six teams playing across the Netherlands and Ireland through September 20
  • The league features heavy Indian involvement, with Rahul Dravid, R Ashwin, and Abhishek Bachchan among owners and players

Former India captain Ajinkya Rahane has signed with the Amsterdam Flames for the inaugural European T20 Premier League, marking a swift return to competitive cricket just days after announcing his retirement from all formats on July 30.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=12rxNKRAy9M

A New Chapter After Retirement

Rahane, 38, ended his international career with 5,077 runs in 85 Tests at an average of 38.46, including 12 centuries. He also scored 2,962 runs in 90 ODIs and appeared in 212 IPL matches across six franchises. His most celebrated achievement was leading India to a Border-Gavaskar Trophy series win in Australia in 2020-21, orchestrating a comeback after India's 36 all-out in Adelaide.

""The reality of life is that everything has a beginning and everything has an end."

"The reality of life is that everything has a beginning and everything has an end. When the time comes, you simply have to respect it and move forward. I have always relied on timing in my batting and have always understood its importance."

— Ajinkya Rahane, in his retirement announcement

The Amsterdam Flames are owned by former Australian captain Steve Waugh alongside field hockey legend Jamie Dwyer and businessman Tim Thomas. The franchise already boasts a strong roster including Mitchell Marsh as captain, Steve Smith, Tim David, Scott Edwards, and Nepal's Dipendra Singh Airee.

Europe's Newest Cricket Frontier

The ETPL, co-founded by Bollywood actor Abhishek Bachchan, Saurav Banerjee, Priyanka Kaul, and Dheeraj Malhotra, kicks off on August 26 at Voorburg Cricket Club in The Hague. The six-team tournament runs through September 20, with matches also scheduled at Malahide in Ireland.

The league features a double round-robin format of 30 matches, with the table-toppers qualifying directly for the final. Indian cricket royalty is heavily involved: Rahul Dravid co-owns the Dublin Guardians, captained by Ravichandran Ashwin, while Glenn Maxwell leads the Belfast Wolves.

"To me, Europe is the last frontier of cricket, and that's why I'm involved."

— Steve Waugh, co-owner, Amsterdam Flames

Other international stars confirmed for the ETPL include Faf du Plessis, Heinrich Klaasen, Trent Boult, Lungi Ngidi, and Mitchell Santner. Each team carries a core of domestic players from the Netherlands, Ireland, and Scotland alongside the international marquee signings.

Rahane's Legacy and Future

Former India cricketer Pravin Amre, Rahane's longtime coach, indicated the veteran still has cricket left in him. "Personally, I feel he still has a year or two of cricket left in him and could play in various leagues around the world," Amre told ANI. "His vast experience — 85 Test matches and 200 IPL games — will be invaluable."

The ETPL represents cricket's growing footprint in Europe and offers Rahane an opportunity to compete at a high level while potentially transitioning into coaching — a path he has expressed interest in pursuing.
nri_angle: The ETPL's deep Indian involvement — from Dravid and Ashwin to Bachchan's co-founding role — makes it compelling viewing for NRIs in Europe and worldwide, while Rahane's post-retirement move underscores Indian cricket's global expansion.
